factors.name: Volume_Rank_Price_Shock_Reversal_20D
factors.description: Structurally distinct variant of the reversal hypothesis that replaces the z-score gate on volume with a time-series rank gate (volume in the top decile of its own trailing 20 days) and replaces the price z-score gate with a simpler within-stock shock test (|return| exceeding the 20-day standard deviation of returns). On qualifying days the factor equals the negative of that day's return, capturing short-horizon reversal after volume and price shock events.
factors.hypothesis: For each CSI500 stock on day t, compute ret_z=(ret-ts_mean(ret,20))/ts_std(ret,20) and vol_z=(volume-ts_mean(volume,20))/ts_std(volume,20) using only past data; define F=-ret*I(vol_z>1 and abs(ret_z)>1) else 0; this conditional short-term reversal factor should positively predict next 5-day returns after abnormal volume and price shocks.
factors.mechanism: Abnormal volume plus price shock can proxy for attention-driven or liquidity-driven overreaction, making a conditional negative-return signal economically plausible while avoiding cross-stock raw-volume comparisons. If a CSI500 stock has a large daily price move accompanied by abnormal within-stock volume, then subsequent short-horizon returns tend to reverse; when the volume shock or price shock is normal, the reversal effect is weaker.
factors.expectedDirection: positive cross-sectional Rank IC for the stated forward horizon
falsificationCriteria: Universe CSI500; daily t; rolling window 20 with min_periods=20 and no future data; vol_z and ret_z normalized per instrument; shock thresholds vol_z>1.0 and abs(ret_z)>1.0; signal F_t=-ret_t on shock days else 0; formula length under 200 characters; test IC and decile spread for forward 5-day return; expected sign positive.
The effect is unstable across years or redundant with an existing factor
factors.statusReason: Canonical Aster diagnostics passed research readiness gates; predictive merit remains subject to Factor Council review

factors.name: Conditional_Reversal_Vol_Price_Shock_20D
factors.description: Direct implementation of the conditional short-term reversal hypothesis: on days when both the 20-day volume shock (vol_z > 1) and the 20-day price shock (|ret_z| > 1) occur, the factor equals the negative of the day's return (betting on reversal); otherwise it is zero. Raw signals are neutralized on normal days so the factor only fires on abnormal-volatility, abnormal-volume overreaction events.

factors.name: Soft_Shock_Weighted_Reversal_20D
factors.description: A softened variant of the conditional reversal signal. Instead of a hard binary indicator, the negative return is continuously weighted by how far the 20-day volume shock and the 20-day price shock exceed the unit threshold (rectified at zero). This retains the economic logic of attention-driven overreaction while avoiding the sharp threshold that can cause instability in parameter choice.

decision.rationale: The chair selects the declared fallback pair. conventional_low_vol has the strongest evidence: mean rank IC 0.0642, ICIR 0.344, positive yearly IC in all years 2016-2025, very low turnover 0.029, and low max abs correlation 0.135. conventional_reversal is the required fallback group with modest but stable positive evidence: mean rank IC 0.0170, ICIR 0.107, positive in 9 of 10 years, 2025 IC 0.040, and adequate coverage. conventional_momentum is not selected despite one reviewer supporting it for a stable negative sign, because the other reviewers prefer disabling it, its sign would require downstream sign learning, and its 0.427 correlation with conventional_reversal reduces incremental value. close_pressure and shock_reversal are disabled because their ICs are near zero (roughly -0.003 and 0.005), turnover is high near 0.33, and their mutual 0.703 correlation indicates redundancy. volume_confirmed_momentum is disabled because reviewers consistently abstained or saw weak, sign-unstable evidence. Using only the fixed fallback groups keeps the mask valid under the required-at-least-one constraint and avoids relying on internally inconsistent non-fallback evidence.
decision.fallbackReason: Reviewer disagreement on conventional_momentum and weak, redundant, or sign-unstable evidence for the other non-fallback candidates make the declared fallback groups the most defensible valid mask.
dissent: factor_evidence_reviewer voted to enable conventional_momentum, citing its persistent negative IC and low turnover; the chair does not include it because the other reviewers favor disabling it and its correlation with conventional_reversal reduces independent contribution.

market_regime_reviewer and risk_data_reviewer favored disabling conventional_momentum, while factor_evidence_reviewer favored enabling it; this split supports using the fallback rather than adding momentum.

market_regime_reviewer abstained on close_pressure and shock_reversal, while factor_evidence_reviewer and risk_data_reviewer voted to disable them; the chair disables both because weak IC and high redundancy dominate.
All reviewers abstained on or did not support enabling volume_confirmed_momentum; the chair disables it given weak and sign-unstable evidence.

ballots.summary: Enable conventional_low_vol and conventional_reversal as core/fallback exposures, and conventional_momentum with lower confidence for its stable negative sign; disable close_pressure and shock_reversal for weak near-zero IC and high redundancy/turnover; abstain on volume_confirmed_momentum pending stronger sign stability. This keeps at least the required fallback exposure and avoids over-weighting weak or redundant groups.

votes.rationale: Mean rank IC -0.0029 and ICIR -0.032 are near zero, yearly sign is mixed, turnover 0.330 is high, and max abs correlation 0.703 with shock_reversal suggests redundancy; no clear persistent incremental signal.
risks: Near-zero IC could still contain noisy sign information, but evidence is too weak for inclusion.
High correlation with shock_reversal makes incremental contribution questionable.

votes.rationale: Mean rank IC 0.0642 and ICIR 0.344, positive in all 10 years, turnover 0.029 very low, and max abs correlation 0.135 low; this is the strongest and most persistent candidate.
risks: 2025 rank IC 0.025 is weaker than the long-run mean.
Low-volatility exposure can be regime-sensitive despite persistent historical evidence.

votes.rationale: Mean rank IC -0.0356 and ICIR -0.208 with negative IC in every year 2016-2025, and turnover 0.071 is low; the stable negative sign can be learned downstream, though correlation 0.427 with conventional_reversal limits incremental information.
risks: Negative raw IC requires the downstream model to learn an inverse sign.
Max abs correlation 0.427 with conventional_reversal reduces independent contribution.

votes.rationale: Mean rank IC 0.0170 and ICIR 0.107, positive in 9 of 10 years with 2023 only slightly negative, and turnover 0.143 is moderate; a fallback group with persistent but modest positive evidence.
risks: Absolute IC is modest and 2023 was marginally negative.
Correlation 0.427 with conventional_momentum means some signal overlap.

votes.rationale: Mean rank IC 0.0050 and ICIR 0.055 are weak despite positive yearly signs, turnover 0.328 is high, and max abs correlation 0.703 with close_pressure suggests redundancy; signal is too small and costly for inclusion.
risks: Positive sign is stable but economically very weak.
High turnover and redundancy make net incremental value doubtful.

votes.rationale: Mean rank IC -0.0179 and ICIR -0.165 imply a potentially learnable negative signal with low turnover 0.098 and low max correlation 0.135, but sign is positive in 2023 and 2025 and absolute IC is weaker; evidence is not strong enough to add beyond the fallback groups.
risks: Sign is not fully stable in recent years.
Weak absolute IC may not survive after transaction costs despite low turnover.

dissentConditions: If conventional_momentum's negative sign reverses or its correlation with conventional_reversal rises materially, revisit its enable vote.
If volume_confirmed_momentum maintains negative IC across the next year with fewer sign flips, reconsider enabling it.
If close_pressure or shock_reversal show sustained ICIR improvement and lower turnover, revisit their disable votes.

ballots.summary: Regime as of 2025-12-31: SH000905 20d return +6.7% but only 19.6% of names above their 60d average, 20d volatility 14.7%, dispersion 13.2%, and average pairwise correlation 0.19. This is a narrow, high-dispersion rally; defensive low-vol and reversal mechanisms are most plausible. Enable conventional_low_vol and conventional_reversal, disable conventional_momentum, and abstain on close_pressure, shock_reversal, and volume_confirmed_momentum. The enabled set satisfies the required fallback coverage via conventional_low_vol and conventional_reversal.

votes.rationale: Near-zero rank IC (-0.003) with high max correlation (0.70) and 33% turnover; in a narrow, high-dispersion rally the short-horizon close-pressure mechanism is not clearly aligned with the regime, so evidence is too weak to enable or disable.
risks: High overlap with shock_reversal may duplicate exposure
Microstructure noise in a low-correlation regime

votes.rationale: Positive and stable rank IC (0.064 mean, 0.34 IR), high positive fraction, very low turnover and correlation; with moderate benchmark volatility, low breadth and high dispersion, the defensive low-vol mechanism is economically plausible as investors favor stability amid a narrow rally.
risks: Low-vol may lag if breadth broadens and risk appetite rises
Crowding risk not inferred from correlation alone

votes.rationale: Rank IC is persistently negative (-0.036 mean, -0.208 IR; 2025 -0.080) and positive fraction is only 42.6%; in a low-breadth, high-dispersion rally, chasing recent winners looks fragile and the observed sign is consistent with reversal rather than momentum, so I would not enable this group in the current regime.
risks: Downstream model could learn negative sign, so disabling may forgo information
A regime shift to broad trending markets could restore momentum

votes.rationale: Rank IC is positive (0.017 mean, 0.107 IR; 2025 0.040) and the fallback reversal mechanism fits a narrow, high-dispersion rally where extended names are more likely to mean-revert; turnover is moderate and correlation is not extreme.
risks: Reversal can fail if the rally broadens into sustained trend
Moderate IC strength

votes.rationale: Rank IC is only 0.005 with 33% turnover and 0.70 max correlation; the post-shock reversal mechanism could fit high dispersion, but the signal is too weak and overlapping to support a confident enable or disable in this regime.
risks: High turnover and overlap with close_pressure
Weak IC may be noise

votes.rationale: Mean rank IC is negative (-0.018) with IR -0.165 and positive fraction 42.3%; volume-confirmed momentum is not clearly supported in a low-breadth rally, but the evidence is not strong enough to rule it out given possible sign learning.
risks: Negative IC may reflect crowded momentum unwinds
Regime-dependent volume confirmation

dissentConditions: If breadth above the 60d average rises materially and pairwise correlation increases, momentum and volume-confirmed momentum should be reconsidered.
If benchmark volatility spikes well above the recent range, low-vol may become crowded or fail despite its historical stability.
If updated factor diagnostics show stronger positive momentum IC, the disable vote for conventional_momentum should be revisited because the downstream model may learn sign.

ballots.summary: As risk/data reviewer, I would enable the two declared fallback baselines: conventional_low_vol (strong, low-turnover, low-correlation) and conventional_reversal (adequate fallback, modest but stable). Disable close_pressure and shock_reversal due weak IC, high turnover, and 0.703 mutual redundancy. Disable conventional_momentum and abstain on volume_confirmed_momentum because their negative/weak IC may be learnable but sign stability and redundancy are not sufficiently supported; prefer fallback groups. All included groups clear coverage >=0.75 and obs >=24, with current labels and no warnings.

votes.rationale: Coverage and observations are adequate (99.4%, 2,180), but mean rank IC is essentially zero (-0.0029) with IR -0.032 and positive fraction 48.5%; turnover is high at 33.0% and max |corr| 0.703 indicates redundancy with shock_reversal. Incremental value is not supported after cost and multiple-testing risk.
risks: High turnover and transaction-cost drag
Collinearity/redundancy with shock_reversal
Near-zero IC may be noise from multiple testing
